correctness.rationale: Explicit Kraus reconstruction yields a single two-by-two phase-sensitive corner block, with QFI 2n²Q/(1+Q+R). For two coordinates with fixed sum and product t, differentiation of (1+Dt)/(C(1-s+t)) has strictly negative numerator D(1-s)-1 in the open cube, proving smoothing monotonicity and hence Schur-concavity and exact extrema. The two SQL boundaries are elementary strict inequalities; the upper envelope threshold is unique by monotonicity. Analytic logarithm/Taylor expansion gives the asymptotic. Full independent spectral-density calculations on 48 instances, 1200 pair smoothings, 2750 envelope tests, 38 threshold tests, and six large-n expansions all passed. Rank-deficient boundaries follow by continuity; no numerical experiment is treated as a proof.

originality.rationale: A recent paper by Farokhi treats distributed GHZ phase sensing but no damping allocation. Bugalho et al. (2024/2025) explicitly give the general inhomogeneous GHZ amplitude-damped matrix and QFI, and Ma et al. (2011) derive homogeneous amplitude-damping precision and the leading SQL threshold: these are acknowledged prior premises, not new results. Koczor et al. (2020) optimize different input probes against fixed channel noise, not allocate fixed aggregate damping over a fixed GHZ state. The compared sources do not assert the fixed-budget strict majorization ordering, complete extremal profiles, and sharp three-region SQL phase partition. Targeted searches did not identify a published equivalent, but the 2024 formula makes a short implicit derivation possible, leaving priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2024 inhomogeneous QFI formula could make equivalent fixed-sum extrema implicit in uninspected passages or other publications.
Electronic semantic search cannot rule out an unpublished, unindexed or differently titled earlier proof.
The ideal noiseless product SQL comparison is not a quantum-advantage claim relative to the optimized noisy local sensing protocol.

value.rationale: A natural aggregate site-decay statistic does not specify spatial heterogeneity. The proof yields exact global best/worst allocations and two distinct design cutoffs. In one regime all allocations beat the ideal separable benchmark; in another only suitable allocation profiles do; in a third none can. The abrupt zero-information option when a single site is fully damped demonstrates that average damping alone is insufficient for performance prediction. This is a structural all-register classification and sharp boundary, not merely another evaluation of the known inhomogeneous QFI expression; model and benchmark limitations are disclosed.
